dish: The original Chicago deep-dish pizza
w: Where Ike Sewell's 1943 pizzeria is credited with launching Chicago deep dish — the original still stands at Ohio & Wabash.

dish: Chicken Vesuvio and steaks amid Cubs memorabilia
w: River North steakhouse (1987) named for the Cubs broadcaster, in a building once home to Capone enforcer Frank Nitti.

dish: Prime USDA steaks and towering cake slices
w: Rush Street power steakhouse since 1989 — consistently among the top-grossing independent restaurants in the US.

dish: The 'Garbage Plate' breakfast in a 1926 railroad lunch car
w: One of America's oldest continuously operating lunch-car diners (1926), hauled to Kenosha by six horses — on the National Register.

dish: Frozen custard cones and sundaes at a 1942 neon drive-in
w: Milwaukee's neon-lit custard stand since the 1940s — said to have inspired Arnold's on Happy Days.

address: 4629 N Port Washington Rd, Glendale, WI 53212
dish: The original butter burger, steamed and topped with Wisconsin butter
w: Glendale diner (1936) thought to have created the Wisconsin butter burger.

address: N Clark St just north of Foster Ave, Andersonville, Chicago
dish: House-made Swedish glögg under the martini-sipping-herring sign
w: The 'Anchor of Andersonville' since 1934 — founded by Swedish immigrant Simon Lundberg over his Prohibition-era No Name Club speakeasy.

dish: Guava-and-cream-cheese pastries, café con leche, pressed medianoches
w: Puerto Rican-owned bakery-café on Paseo Boricua a block from Humboldt Park — some of the city's best Puerto Rican coffee and pastries.

dish: Al pastor tacos on house tortillas and a deep bourbon list
w: Paul Kahan's honky-tonk taco and whiskey bar at the Damen-Milwaukee crossroads of Wicker Park, with its packed summer patio.

dish: Daisy Cutter pale ale and fresh IPAs at the brewery taproom
w: The big Balmoral brewery and taproom (2017) of Half Acre, a staple of Chicago craft brewing since 2006.

dish: Live country bands, pool, cheap beer and hot sandwiches
w: Uptown's late-night honky-tonk — one of Chicago's last straight-up country bars, closed in 2016 and revived in 2018.

dish: Irish whiskey shots and cheap beer
w: Lakeview dive at Clark & Belmont since the 1950s — Irish whiskey selection, a dark lore, and a stop on Anthony Bourdain's The Layover.

dish: Chicken tinga huarache on hand-patted masa
w: Six-table Edgewater counter where masa is patted and griddled to order — called the best huaraches in Chicago. Cash only.

dish: Carne asada tacos with fiery salsa verde
w: Cash-only North Center taqueria — 'some of the freshest tacos in town' (Time Out); the Infatuation rates its carne asada 8.1.

dish: Heritage pork chop, a 20–30-variety oyster list, Belgian-leaning beer
w: Paul Kahan's 2008 Fulton Market beer hall of pork, oysters and beer — the restaurant that helped turn the meatpacking district into a dining destination.

dish: Old-school Tuscan-American pastas and veal in a twinkle-lit 'village' dining room
w: Chicago's oldest Italian restaurant (1927), opened by Lucca-born Alfredo Capitanini and run by the fourth generation — a pre-opera Loop institution.

dish: Hand-rolled pastas from the open pastificio counter (cacio whey pepe, ragù alla Napoletana)
w: James Beard-winning chef Sarah Grueneberg's West Loop pasta house (2015), with sheets rolled and hung daily in view of the counter.

dish: Chicago-style hot dogs and shakes under 1960 neon
w: Beverly's neon-trimmed 1960 drive-in, revived in 2014 with its classic décor and menu intact — featured on Chicago's Best.

dish: Whiskey flights, old fashioneds and nose-to-tail plates
w: The 'Eat Sleep Whisky' gastropub-inn that put Logan Square on the dining map (Condé Nast Traveler); Michelin-listed in 2024.

dish: Jibaritos (plantain 'bread') with churrasco, plus a dozen kinds of mofongo
w: Yelitza Rivera's Logan Square corner (2016) with the widest jibarito menu in town — lines out the door, now with a sit-down room next door.

dish: Wood-fired Neapolitan pizza from a custom oak-fired oven
w: Ravenswood's Neapolitan pizzeria with a quiet side-street patio — No. 14 in 50 Top Pizza USA 2023 and on its world top-100.

dish: Barbecued ribs and late-night pub plates under celebrity photos
w: Loop pub since 1935 under the Wabash 'L' — signed photos from Sinatra to Monroe and one of the Loop's few late-night kitchens.

address: Randolph St at Peoria St, West Loop, Chicago
dish: The Mr. G sub — provolone, prosciutto, Genoa, hot sopressata, truffle-mustard vinaigrette
w: Italian grocer since 1937, now in its fourth generation — its walk-up sub counter turns out some of the best sandwiches in the city.

address: N Michigan Ave between Lake & Randolph (Millennium Park Plaza), Chicago
dish: The Chicago (Garrett) Mix — CaramelCrisp and CheeseCorn in one bag
w: Chicago's popcorn icon since 1949 — the caramel-cheddar mix invented by customers in the 1970s; the Michigan Avenue shop's queue is a tourist-board photo.

dish: Sambusas, shimbra asa and stews in 'Diamond berbere'
w: Edgewater's Ethiopian dining room — the oldest Ethiopian restaurant in Chicago, nearly three decades on Broadway.
